A2b-spirogyra

A magnified horizontal view of a short length of a Spirogyra filament: three cylindrical cells joined end to end in a straight row. Each cell has a thin cellulose wall, one spiral ribbon-shaped green chloroplast coiling around the inside with small round pyrenoids along it, a large clear central vacuole, and a nucleus suspended in the centre of the cell by fine thin cytoplasmic strands. A faint transparent mucilage sheath around the outside of the whole filament. Soft greens. Plenty of white space above and below.
A2b-spirogyra-conjugation

Two horizontal Spirogyra filaments lying parallel, one above the other, joined by short straight conjugation tubes between matching cells like the rungs of a ladder (scalariform conjugation). In the upper filament the green cell contents are rounded up into balls, and in one cell the contents are shown squeezing through a tube downwards. In the lower filament several cells each contain one dark brown oval thick-walled zygospore. Soft greens with dark brown zygospores.
A2b-moss

Left: a moss plant: a small upright leafy green shoot (gametophyte) with tiny spirally arranged leaves and thin brown rhizoids at the base; from its tip grows a long thin brown stalk (seta) ending in an oval capsule covered by a pointed hood-like cap (calyptra). Right, clearly separated: an enlarged moss capsule with the lid removed, showing a ring of pointed peristome teeth around its open mouth and tiny spores. Soft greens and browns.
A2b-moss-life-cycle

A circular life cycle of a moss, with plain curved arrows going clockwise between seven separate small pictures evenly spaced around a circle: top: tiny round spores; then a green branched thread (protonema) on soil; then a group of small leafy moss shoots with rhizoids; then two shoot tips side by side, a male tip with club-shaped antheridia releasing tiny swimming sperm and a female tip with flask-shaped archegonia; then a single round zygote inside a flask-shaped archegonium; then a female leafy shoot with a sporophyte (thin seta and capsule) growing out of its tip; then a capsule opening and releasing spores. Soft greens and browns.
A2b-marchantia

Three Marchantia plants side by side with white space between them. Left: a flat, green, ribbon-like thallus lying on soil, branching into two again and again (dichotomous branching), with fine rhizoids underneath and several small round cup-shaped gemma cups on its upper surface, each holding tiny green discs (gemmae). Middle: a male thallus with an upright stalk carrying a flat, lobed, disc-shaped head (antheridiophore). Right: a female thallus with an upright stalk carrying an umbrella of finger-like rays (archegoniophore). Soft greens.
A2b-fern

Left: a fern plant (Dryopteris type) with a horizontal underground rhizome covered in brown scales, many thin adventitious roots below it, three large feathery compound fronds above, and one young tightly coiled frond (fiddlehead) unrolling. Show the soil line. Right top, clearly separated: an enlarged view of the underside of one leaflet (pinnule) with two rows of round brown sori, each partly covered by a kidney-shaped flap (indusium). Right bottom: one enlarged stalked sporangium, a flattened capsule with a curved ring of thick-walled cells (annulus) along its edge, releasing spores. Soft greens and browns.
A2b-fern-life-cycle

A circular life cycle of a fern with plain curved arrows going clockwise between seven separate small pictures evenly spaced around a circle: top: a mature fern plant (sporophyte); then the underside of a frond leaflet with brown sori; then a single sporangium bursting and releasing spores; then a single spore germinating; then a small flat heart-shaped green prothallus with rhizoids; then the underside of the prothallus showing small round antheridia near the rhizoids releasing swimming sperm and flask-shaped archegonia near the notch; then a young fern with its first small frond and root growing out of the prothallus. Soft greens and browns.
A2b-gymnosperms

Two gymnosperms side by side with white space between. Left: a cycad with a stout, rough, unbranched trunk, a crown of stiff, palm-like pinnate leaves, and one large upright cone in the centre of the crown. Right: a pine branch with long needle-like leaves in bundles, a cluster of small soft male cones near the branch tip, a larger woody female cone with spiral scales, and beside the branch a single winged pine seed. Soft greens and browns.
A2b-maize-waterleaf

Two whole plants side by side, clearly separated, roots shown in a cut-away of the soil. Left: a maize plant with a fibrous root system and a few prop roots from the lowest nodes, a tall unbranched stem with visible nodes, long narrow parallel-veined leaves, a tassel (male flowers) at the top, and one cob with silky hairs in a leaf axil. Right: a waterleaf plant (Talinum) with a single tap root and side roots, soft fleshy green branching stems, broad oval fleshy leaves with net veins, and a few small pink five-petalled flowers. Soft greens and yellows.
A2b-flowering-plant-life-cycle

A circular life cycle of a flowering plant with plain curved arrows going clockwise between seven separate pictures evenly spaced around a circle: top: a bean seed; then a germinating seed with a small root and shoot; then a young seedling in soil; then a mature flowering plant; then a close-up of a flower with a bee on it carrying pollen; then a cut-away of a pistil with a pollen tube growing down the style into an ovule; then a pod-like fruit opened to show seeds. Soft greens, yellows and pinks.
A2b-annual-biennial-perennial

Three horizontal rows separated by white space, each a timeline running left to right with plain arrows. Top row (annual): a maize seed, then a young maize plant, then a tall maize plant with tassel and cob, then a dry dead maize plant. Middle row (biennial): a carrot plant with leaves and a swollen orange root, then the same plant with a tall flowering stalk of white flower heads, then a dead dried carrot plant. Bottom row (perennial): the same mango tree shown three times getting bigger each time, each one with flowers and green and yellow mangoes. Soft greens, oranges and browns.
A2b-plant-evolution

A left-to-right landscape showing plants rising like steps from water onto land. Far left: a pond with green Spirogyra filaments floating in the water. Next: a damp rock with a moss clump and a flat Marchantia thallus. Next: a fern in shady damp ground. Next: a cycad and a pine tree on drier land. Far right: a maize plant and a small flowering waterleaf plant on dry land. A gentle staircase of ground rising from the water on the left to dry land on the right. Each group clearly separated. Soft greens, blues and browns.
